brief: Henry Williams was born in 1792 and served in the Royal Navy. From 1823 he became the leader of the CMS missionaries from his base at Paihia. He became renowned for his often successful mediation in inter-tribal fighting. As conversions increased Williams supervised the establishment of several new mission stations. He strongly supported the Treaty of Waitangi, and was official interpreter at the first signing. He was unfairly criticized by Governor Grey for his land purchases on behalf of his family, but served the Māori people for over forty years until his death in 1867.
